hero.lead: A nation of 175.7 million on the world’s largest delta, where four in five now live above $4.20 a day and the World Bank committed $1.1 billion to protect food security in 2026.

capital.heading: Bangladesh has carried its people through shock after shock. Next, a clean stove in every home.

record.text: Emergency support for food security and livelihoods: Food security and livelihoods
Financial Sector Support Project II: Deposit insurance and bank supervision
New IMF-supported programme (requested): Size to be set in negotiation

register.name: Emergency support for food security and livelihoods
register.text: Protects households from the fuel and food shocks of 2026.

register.name: Financial Sector Support Project II
register.text: Protects small savers and strengthens the central bank’s supervision.

register.name: Health, Nutrition and Population Sector Development Program
register.detail: Signed 10 June 2026 · 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2029 · Two projects
register.note: IDA credit of SDR 284.70 million and a $25 million GFF grant
register.text: Two projects under the national health programme: one strengthens health and nutrition services across the country, with a focus on the Chattogram and Sylhet divisions; the other improves climate-resilient reproductive health and population services.

register.name: New IMF-supported programme (requested)
register.note: Size to be set in negotiation
register.text: Follows the ECF, EFF and RSF arrangements approved in January 2023.

register.name: Energy Sector Security Enhancement Project, Additional Financing
register.detail: Approved 15 May 2026 · IDA payment guarantee · Original project approved 18 June 2025
register.text: An IDA payment guarantee-backed facility of standby letters of credit and short-term credit lines for Petrobangla’s LNG imports, so that it can contract supply for longer and rely less on costly spot purchases. It supports more reliable electricity.

register.name: Modernising social protection
register.text: Modernises the social protection system for the poorest families.

register.name: Inclusive Affordable Housing Finance Project
register.detail: Approved 27 September 2026 · Signed 7 October 2026 · Concessional loan
register.note: Home loans for at least 40,000 households by 2031
register.text: Long-term, collateral-free microfinance loans, through PKSF and microfinance institutions, for families with informal incomes to build, repair and upgrade their homes, with disaster-resilient design. The 40,000 households are to include at least 32,000 women.

register.name: Sustainable Energy Development and Community Empowerment in the Chattogram Hill Tracts
register.note: Power for at least 88,000 more households in 26 upazilas
register.text: New and modernised distribution networks in Khagrachari, Rangamati and Bandarban: 5,032 km of new lines, six new substations, at least 30 solar-powered drinking water facilities, and solar backup for schools, clinics and other community buildings.

register.name: Strengthening Economic Management and Governance Program, Subprogram 2
register.detail: Signed June 2026 · Policy-based loan · With the Asian Development Bank
register.note: Part of a proposed $750 million AIIB package
register.text: Budget support from AIIB’s Emergency Response Support Facility, jointly with ADB, to maintain macroeconomic stability and advance structural reforms as the conflicts in the Middle East weigh on the economy.

register.name: Narayanganj Green and Resilient Urban Development Project
register.note: Water and drainage for at least 400,000 residents
register.text: Replaces and extends 230 km of water pipeline, adds metered household connections and raises supply from 113 to 162 million litres a day, with 22 km of drainage built with nature-based solutions and new green parks.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 33 in every hundred live in towns and cities; the rest live on the land they farm and fish.
items.alt: A busy street in Dhaka with cycle rickshaws

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in farms and pasture
items.text: The land that feeds the nation, and the first place a citizen dividend can be earned.
items.alt: Green rice paddies in the Bangladesh delta at harvest time

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest
items.text: Standing forest holds the water, soil and carbon that the world will pay to keep.
items.alt: The Sundarbans mangrove forest, Bangladesh, tidal channels between the trees

items.name: The Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water per person
items.text: Below the scarcity line of 1,000 cubic metres: every drop must be stored, treated and reused.
items.alt: A wide river in the Bangladesh delta with wooden country boats

items.name: The Power
items.label: Of energy from renewables, 2021
items.text: Sun, wind, water and biomass already carry part of the load; the rest is the opportunity.
items.alt: A solar home system on a rural house roof in Bangladesh

items.name: iFarmer
items.text: Finance, advice, farm inputs and buyers for smallholders: the company says it works with over 300,000 farmers and 24,000 farm retailers.

items.name: Drinkwell
items.text: Runs 302 Water ATM kiosks in Dhaka with Dhaka WASA; more than 750,000 families hold its prepaid water cards.

items.name: SOLshare
items.text: Links solar home systems so neighbours can trade surplus power; about 40% of its customers were first-time electricity users.
